subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Bubble Tea's Rise
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bubble Tea's Rise usable.

hook.text: In 1980s Taiwan, a tea shop owner dropped tapioca balls into iced milk tea. A phenomenon was born.

buildup.text: The chewy tapioca pearls added a playful texture that no other drink offered. Young people loved it.

discovery.text: Two Taiwanese tea shops both claim to have invented it. The dispute has never been legally resolved.

twist.text: Bubble tea swept across Asia in the 1990s and hit Western cities in the 2010s, becoming a $4 billion industry.

climax.text: Today, global chains like Gong Cha and Tiger Sugar have thousands of locations on six continents.

punchline.text: Tapioca in tea. Simple idea, global empire.

details.summary: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan in the 1980s when tapioca pearls were added to iced milk tea. What started as a local novelty became a global phenomenon, particularly popular with young people across Asia, North America, and Europe. The bubble tea industry is now worth billions of dollars.
details.whyItMatters: Bubble tea represents tea's ability to reinvent itself for new generations. It turned a traditional drink into a playful, customizable, and Instagram-worthy experience.
takeaways: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan in the 1980s
Tapioca pearls added to milk tea created the signature drink
It has become a global multi-billion dollar industry

faq.question: Who actually invented bubble tea?
faq.answer: Two Taiwanese tea shop owners both claim credit: Liu Han-Chieh of Chun Shui Tang and Tu Tsong-He of Hanlin Tea Room. Both were experimenting with cold tea and tapioca in the 1980s. The true origin is disputed, but Taiwan is universally recognized as bubble tea's birthplace.

faq.question: Why has bubble tea become so popular globally?
faq.answer: Its combination of sweet tea, chewy tapioca pearls, and endless customization options appeals to younger consumers. The visual appeal makes it social media friendly. Asian diaspora communities spread it globally, and the novelty factor continues to attract new customers.
